newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Cadbury Schweppes eyes S. African bottler assets.
newsitem.headline: Cadbury Schweppes eyes S. African bottler assets.

text.p: Food and drinks group Cadbury Schweppes (South Africa) Ltd (Cadswep) said on Tuesday it was considering buying bottling equipment belonging to local firm New Age Beverages Ltd (NAB) currently under provisional liquidation.

Managing director David Jackson said the local Cadswep unit had forwarded details on the possible buys to its U.K.-based parent firm Cadbury Schweppes Plc for it to ascertain if any of its global units were interested in the assets.
"Like everyone else I saw the liquidators. I went and had a look at the machinery in case one of our branches overseas might be interested," he told Reuters.
He said there was no local interest in acquiring NAB's bottling equipment as the firm already had a sound marketing and distribution deal with Coca-Cola Corp for its local brands.
"We (are) simply interested in having a look at it for elsewhere in the world. We are a global company," Jackson added.
NAB, the local bottler and distributor for U.S.-based PepsiCo Inc , applied for voluntary liquidation in May after kicking off a South African division of the global cola wars three years ago.
Liquidators say it has incurred debts amounting to over 400 million rand ($87.8 million) during its battle with its arch-rival Coca-Cola.
NAB had also sprearheaded Pepsi's high-profile return to South Africa following the firm's disinvestment move during the apartheid era.

Les Cohen of Westrust (Pty) Ltd, one of the three joint provisional liquidators, confirmed that Cadswep had approached them about inspecting NAB's bottling equipment, including canning, packaging and filling lines.
"They've come to see the liquidators but I can't be sure if they've seen the plants. I should imagine it's the bottling and canning (plant) equipment they are interested in," he told Reuters.

Cohen said the provisional liquidation order was extended on Tuesday due to NAB's failure to have it published in the government gazette as required by law and placed in the press for public interest.
He said the court moved to pass a final liquidation order on July 29, when the compliance requirements would have been met.
"The company has to go through to final liquidation. It's hopelessly insolvent," Cohen said, adding NAB had one bottling and distribution plant in KwaZulu-Natal and five others in the Gauteng region.
Cadsweps' main operating subsidiaries locally, are Cadbury (Pty) Ltd, Bromor Foods Ltd, Chapelat-Humphries Investments (Pty) Ltd.
